labels: Determine whether acting is for her!

nodes.text: Sam steps forward, smiling.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Tryouts! Tryouts for 'Romeo and Juliet'!

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Ever wanted to perform in a play before? Now's your opportunity!
She hands out flyers to people passing through.

nodes.speaker: Erik
nodes.text: A play? I'd love to do a play! The rush, the thrill, the excitement!

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Have you been in one before?

nodes.speaker: Erik
nodes.text: No, but I'm very versatile! I can be anything you want! Backup dancer, unassuming janitor, a wall...

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Well, we do need side characters... Take one!
Erik takes his happily, and Sam continues to pass out flyers!

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: 'Romeo and Juliet'? Isn't that the romantic one?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Uh, yeah...

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: That means there's kissing! And wherever there's kissing, I'm in!
He takes one before Sam can retract it. The cheerleaders come up...

nodes.speaker: Hector
nodes.text: Hey, free stuff. Great!

nodes.speaker: Amanda
nodes.text: Yay, paper! I love paper!
By the time everyone's come through the doors, Sam has handed out most of her flyers!
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I'm almost out. How'd everyone else do?

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: I'm nearly to the bottom of my stack as well. Kevin?
He thumbs through a still-thick stack of flyers.

nodes.speaker: Kevin
nodes.text: I'm not going to say that being an attractive girl is an advantage when it comes to handing out flyers but...

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: But you think we're attractive?

nodes.speaker: Kevin
nodes.text: What... No? I mean, yes! I was just trying to say, uh...

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Ha ha... At least we have some to staple on the bulletin boards in the school hallway.

nodes.speaker: Andrew
nodes.text: They're not interested.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: They can decide for themselves.

nodes.speaker: Andrew
nodes.text: Well, it... It doesn't matter! Whether or not they want to, they'll be `busy.`
nodes.text_bbcode: Well, it... It doesn't matter! Whether or not they want to, they'll be [color=#e23b3b][i]busy.[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Hannah
nodes.text: With what?

nodes.speaker: Andrew
nodes.text: There's a rehearsal today after school.

nodes.speaker: Ashley
nodes.text: What? But that's not on the sched--

nodes.speaker: Andrew
nodes.text: It's an `emergency` rehearsal, and if you still want to be in `my` production, then you'll `be there.`
nodes.text_bbcode: It's an [color=#e23b3b][i]emergency[/i][/color] rehearsal, and if you still want to be in [color=#e23b3b][i]my[/i][/color] production, then you'll [color=#e23b3b][i]be there.[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: You just made that up right now!

nodes.speaker: Andrew
nodes.text: `Or...` I just happened to think of something I wanted to change right now!
nodes.text_bbcode: [color=#e23b3b][i]Or...[/i][/color] I just happened to think of something I wanted to change right now!

nodes.speaker: Andrew
nodes.text: And you can't prove otherwise.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Ugh!

nodes.speaker: Andrew
nodes.text: Ha! You can try to best me, shrew! But, like Shakespeare's Petruchio before me, call me `shrew-tamer!`
nodes.text_bbcode: Ha! You can try to best me, shrew! But, like Shakespeare's Petruchio before me, call me [color=#e23b3b][i]shrew-tamer![/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Andrew
nodes.text: Consider yourself `tamed.`
nodes.text_bbcode: Consider yourself [color=#e23b3b][i]tamed.[/i][/color]

nodes.text: With that, Andrew turns and leaves.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Well, `that` catch-phrase isn't going on any billboards anytime soon.
nodes.text_bbcode: Well, [color=#3b78e2][i]that[/i][/color] catch-phrase isn't going on any billboards anytime soon.

nodes.text: Ashley and Hannah look mournfully at Sam.

nodes.speaker: Ashley
nodes.text: I'm sorry, Sam...
Sam looks at Ashley and Hannah who sigh in relief.
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: If I told him that they'd approached me, they'd get in trouble with him... Good thing I kept my mouth shut.

nodes.speaker: Andrew
nodes.text: I find that incredibly hard to believe.

nodes.speaker: Hannah
nodes.text: Actually, it's true. Sam and I are total `swim teammates` on the `swimming team,` aren't we?
nodes.text_bbcode: Actually, it's true. Sam and I are total [color=#3b78e2][i]swim teammates[/i][/color] on the [color=#3b78e2][i]swimming team,[/i][/color] aren't we?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Yeah, total `swim`mates. And Ashley's cool too.
nodes.text_bbcode: Yeah, total [color=#3b78e2][i]swim[/i][/color]mates. And Ashley's cool too.

nodes.speaker: Andrew
nodes.text: Uh-huh. I'm `sure.`
nodes.text_bbcode: Uh-huh. I'm [color=#e23b3b][i]sure.[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Look, even if we were talking about plays...

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Which we `weren't.`
nodes.text_bbcode: Which we [color=#3b78e2][i]weren't.[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: It's not against the rules for them to be in `two` productions.
nodes.text_bbcode: It's not against the rules for them to be in [color=#3b78e2][i]two[/i][/color] productions.

nodes.text: Ashley and Hannah's eyes widen, and Sam realizes she should have probably kept that information to herself.
Andrew turns to them furiously.

nodes.speaker: Andrew
nodes.text: Did you approach her?

nodes.speaker: Hannah
nodes.text: It was Ashley's idea!

nodes.speaker: Andrew
nodes.text: Was it really? You know, Ashley, you're the Nurse because I know you're a good actress...

nodes.speaker: Andrew
nodes.text: But it won't take more than a penstroke to take that all away!

nodes.speaker: Ashley
nodes.text: No!

nodes.speaker: Andrew
nodes.text: And while I'm at it, I could make sure that you never work in the drama club again!

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Andrew, stop it... It's not against the rules for them to be in `two` productions.
nodes.text_bbcode: Andrew, stop it... It's not against the rules for them to be in [color=#3b78e2][i]two[/i][/color] productions.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: They, uh... They came to me!

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: I'm game! Besides... Basketball's over, and football's not here yet. I won't have to think of sports if I'm sword-fighting!

nodes.speaker: Kevin
nodes.text: And maybe we can find some tights that you'll like!

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: No tights!

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Just come to auditions! We'll worry about costumes later!
They finish up their lunches, talking with the students at other tables, encouraging them to come.
As they walk to their lockers, Sam sighs.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Do you think everyone will come? What if there aren't any good actors?

nodes.speaker: Kevin
nodes.text: We'll deal with it when we deal with it.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Hm. Strangely truthful.
They're about to head out when Hannah and Ashley find them in the hallway.

nodes.speaker: Ashley
nodes.text: Hey, Sam... Can we talk with you for a second?

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: I'll see you after school, Sam!

nodes.speaker: Kevin
nodes.text: Ditto.
Sam steps aside to talk with Hannah and Ashley.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: What's up?

nodes.speaker: Ashley
nodes.text: We saw some flyers you were passing out today about the auditions.

nodes.speaker: Ashley
nodes.text: Would you be okay if we tried out?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Yeah, I'd be fine! You guys are in the drama club.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: But what about Andrew? Did you guys quit his play?

nodes.speaker: Ashley
nodes.text: Oh, no, we're still in it. I want the experience.

nodes.speaker: Hannah
nodes.text: So do I. That... And it's kind of covering one of my electives. If I drop it, I fail 'Independent Study'.

nodes.speaker: Ashley
nodes.text: But Andrew's a little bit overbearing...

nodes.speaker: Hannah
nodes.text: An actual `bear` couldn't be more overbearing!
nodes.text_bbcode: An actual [color=#3b78e2][i]bear[/i][/color] couldn't be more overbearing!

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Yeah, I got that.

nodes.speaker: Ashley
nodes.text: It'd be nice to be in a production where I'd have some more say as an actress... And I'd like a chance to be a star.

nodes.speaker: Hannah
nodes.text: I just don't want to be `Jenna's backup.` It's just sad.
nodes.text_bbcode: I just don't want to be [color=#3b78e2][i]Jenna's backup.[/i][/color] It's just sad.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: So... You guys want to tryout for my play, but you need to be in his too? I could `try` to work around that...
nodes.text_bbcode: So... You guys want to tryout for my play, but you need to be in his too? I could [color=#3b78e2][i]try[/i][/color] to work around that...

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: But you'd really need to run it by Andrew first. I don't want him to think that I'm poaching any of his--

nodes.speaker: Ashley
nodes.text: Oh, great! We knew you could keep it a `secret!`
nodes.text_bbcode: Oh, great! We knew you could keep it a [color=#3b78e2][i]secret![/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Hannah
nodes.text: You're the best!

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: No! That's the opposite of what I--

nodes.speaker: Andrew
nodes.text: `What is this?!`
nodes.text_bbcode: [color=#e23b3b][i]What is this?![/i][/color]

nodes.text: Andrew steps in Sam's face.

nodes.speaker: Andrew
nodes.text: Shrew! It's already bad enough that you're gunning for my scholarship...

nodes.speaker: Andrew
nodes.text: Now you're trying to sabotage me by tearing my entire production apart! You're poaching my actors!
Behind Andrew's back, Hannah and Ashley shake their heads frantically.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I'm not poaching them! They...

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: What are you trying to say?

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: That I need a `play` to meet girls? I know cute girls.
nodes.text_bbcode: That I need a [color=#e23b3b][i]play[/i][/color] to meet girls? I know cute girls.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: They were all over me after we won Sectionals!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Really? Where are they now?

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: They're, uh, they all go to Willow Glen. You don't know them!

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: But what I'm saying is that I don't need help getting a girl.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I just thought you might like `hanging around them` while you're swinging a sword at me as Tybalt--
nodes.text_bbcode: I just thought you might like [color=#3b78e2][i]hanging around them[/i][/color] while you're swinging a sword at me as Tybalt--

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: `Sword?!` Did you say `sword?` I'm there.
nodes.text_bbcode: [color=#e23b3b][i]Sword?![/i][/color] Did you say [color=#e23b3b][i]sword?[/i][/color] I'm there.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: You'll probably get one of the really awesome parts where you can have a choreographed stage fight.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I know `I'm` excited. Since I'm Tybalt, I'll be in one of those fight scenes too.
nodes.text_bbcode: I know [color=#3b78e2][i]I'm[/i][/color] excited. Since I'm Tybalt, I'll be in one of those fight scenes too.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: And the prop swords in the drama department are nothing to laugh at. They `look` real!
nodes.text_bbcode: And the prop swords in the drama department are nothing to laugh at. They [color=#3b78e2][i]look[/i][/color] real!

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: You can stop talking now. You had me at 'sword'!
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I should have known. Well, it's good to know that I can still guess what you like.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: So are you in or not?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: So the flyers are out. What now?

nodes.speaker: Kevin
nodes.text: Well, like I was saying before, you should start recruiting your friends. That's how most plays are made.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Kevin's right. We should start talking to people personally, starting with the Center Table. Ready to go on over?
They grab their lunches and walk to the Center Table in the cafeteria.

nodes.speaker: Kevin
nodes.text: Uh, I'll try to catch you guys later...

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Why?

nodes.speaker: Kevin
nodes.text: This isn't really my scene. I belong over there.
He points at a table of nerds.

nodes.speaker: Dex
nodes.text: I summon a fireball against your face!

nodes.speaker: Kevin
nodes.text: See there? That fireball's supposed to be in `my` face.
nodes.text_bbcode: See there? That fireball's supposed to be in [color=#e23b3b][i]my[/i][/color] face.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: I didn't realize there was a proper seating order.

nodes.speaker: Kevin
nodes.text: Popular girls usually don't.

nodes.speaker: Kevin
nodes.text: Besides, I don't want to crowd you.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Well, come sit with us now. You're our producer and stagehand. It's only for a day. I'm sure it won't kill you.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Much.
Kevin shrugs and sits with them at the center table.
Around them, the cheerleaders and the jocks chatter happily. $ZOE slides in with Ben, Emily, Kimi, and Spencer.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: 'Sup, Samface!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Hey, $ZOE, Sam...
He looks over and sees Kevin. He brightens.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Kevin, you don't normally come around here...

nodes.speaker: Kevin
nodes.text: We can't all be scientists turned superstars...

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: Yeah, but I'm surprised you're turning down that ogres game you always play with Dex...

nodes.speaker: Kevin
nodes.text: We can't all be ogres either.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Well, it's good to see your face again. What are you up to?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I can answer that. He's helping me with a production of 'Romeo and Juliet'.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Actually, we kind of need your help. It's really important that Sam puts on this play.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Would you guys be interested in trying out?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: It kind of sounds fun...

nodes.speaker: Kimi
nodes.text: And by 'it kind of sounds fun', she means 'heck yeah, we'd `love` to be in a `play!`
nodes.text_bbcode: And by 'it kind of sounds fun', she means 'heck yeah, we'd [color=#3b78e2][i]love[/i][/color] to be in a [color=#3b78e2][i]play![/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Er, yeah, what she said.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Great! And maybe now that basketball season's over, Ben and Spencer would want to join too?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Uh...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Ben would love to!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I would?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Hey, you were just telling me the other day that you kind of missed basketball. This could be fun for you.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: It's for a good cause...

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Well, I can't turn it down now... I'm game.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Well, you can count me out.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: You're not getting me onstage! Not in those girly tights!

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Come on, Spence. I need the help.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Yeah, it'll be fun. 'Romeo and Juliet' is a romantic play set in medieval times.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: That means there'll be...
Sam steps forward... But panic seizes her, and she forgets what to do!
People start streaming past her...

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Uh... Uh...

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Take this!
She tries to hand out a flyer, but accidentally grabs several at once and throws them at a passing student.

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: Hey, hey!

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Sorry!
Realizing it's Sam, Ryan smooths his hair down.

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: Nah, it's okay, Sam... You can throw your papers all over me whenever you--

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Just keep walking, buddy.

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: Walking!
Angry at herself for fumbling, Sam doesn't realize she's scowling at everyone who passes by.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Take a flyer! It's for a play, you idiots!

nodes.speaker: Erik
nodes.text: Wuhh... I'm not supposed to talk to strangers, scary paper monster lady!
Erik ducks under her and runs away. Sam turns to others to hand out more flyers with an angry expression on her face.

nodes.speaker: Hector
nodes.text: Whoa boy, Sam's on a rampage! It's a `Sampage!` Out of the way!
nodes.text_bbcode: Whoa boy, Sam's on a rampage! It's a [color=#e23b3b][i]Sampage![/i][/color] Out of the way!

nodes.text: The people filing in behind Hector avoid her at all costs!
By the time that everyone's come through the doors, Sam is still carrying a thick stack of flyers!
She, $ZOE, and Kevin meet up to talk about how they managed.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Well, I'm nearly to the bottom of my stack. How did everyone else do?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Not that well... I kind of froze up there.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Kevin?

nodes.speaker: Kevin
nodes.text: I didn't do much better than Sam.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Oh, well that's okay... I guess we can always staple the extras to bulletin boards...

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I just hope people will come...
Later that day...
$ZOE and Sam find that no one's made it to their rehearsal!

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Oh no, I can't believe this is happening!

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Maybe it's because everyone's running a little late? I mean, class did just get out.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Class got out twenty minutes ago.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Let's just wait a little longer...
Twenty more minutes pass...

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Maybe people have other clubs they're in.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Maybe.
An hour passes...

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Some people could have gotten lost...

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: They'd have to be `blind` not to see the auditorium from the main buildings...
nodes.text_bbcode: They'd have to be [color=#3b78e2][i]blind[/i][/color] not to see the auditorium from the main buildings...

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Still...
And soon, it's twenty minutes to five o'clock. Sam sighs.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: ...Forget it, $ZOE.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: No one's coming.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Sam, it's not over yet. You still have time. There are other scholarships...

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Yeah. It'll be fine...
But Sam knows in her heart...
She has failed.

nodes.prompt: What do you want to do?

menu.title: Make your choice!
menu.text: What do you want to do?

nodes.speaker: Ms. Macbeth
nodes.text: Excellent idea! Oh, I'm very pleased all around. These will be `wonderful` essays and even more wonderful performances!
nodes.text_bbcode: Excellent idea! Oh, I'm very pleased all around. These will be [color=#3b78e2][i]wonderful[/i][/color] essays and even more wonderful performances!

nodes.speaker: Ms. Macbeth
nodes.text: Anyway, that's it for this meeting. I just need to collect your initial paperwork, and we'll be set.
Andrew and Sam both hand in their paperwork. Ms. Macbeth thumbs through both applications.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Macbeth
nodes.text: Great, Andrew. You're all ready to go.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Macbeth
nodes.text: But Sam... You're missing a cast list. I need that from you.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: A cast list?

nodes.speaker: Ms. Macbeth
nodes.text: Yeah, a list of everyone who'll be in your performance and their roles.

nodes.speaker: Andrew
nodes.text: You `do` know that you can't be the `only` actor in your play, right?
nodes.text_bbcode: You [color=#e23b3b][i]do[/i][/color] know that you can't be the [color=#e23b3b][i]only[/i][/color] actor in your play, right?

nodes.text: Sam fixes him with a withering look before answering Ms. Macbeth.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I didn't know we had to turn that in, and I'm still finalizing some casting, so...

nodes.speaker: Ms. Macbeth
nodes.text: Unfortunately, the deadline is today, so I'll need that from you by 5pm, if that's all right.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Yeah, of course! No problem!

nodes.speaker: Ms. Macbeth
nodes.text: Great.
Sam rushes out of the conference room and runs straight into $ZOE and Kevin who are waiting outside.

nodes.speaker: Kevin
nodes.text: How'd it go?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Big problem!

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Problem? What problem?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Ms. Macbeth needs a cast list by the end of today. I haven't even had enough time to get a cast together, much less to know what everyone's role is!

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: This entire play idea is a train wreck... No, it's a plane collision on top of a train wreck!

nodes.speaker: Andrew
nodes.text: Actually, no... Your play is more like a `cataclysmic intergalactic war` on top of a plane collision on top of a train wreck.
nodes.text_bbcode: Actually, no... Your play is more like a [color=#e23b3b][i]cataclysmic intergalactic war[/i][/color] on top of a plane collision on top of a train wreck.

nodes.text: Sam whips around to glare at Andrew, who's just walked out of the conference room behind her. He chuckles at his own joke.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Geek.

nodes.speaker: Andrew
nodes.text: Jock.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: That's not as much of an insult as you think it is.

nodes.speaker: Andrew
nodes.text: Fine. But you trying to skate by and win this scholarship `is` an insult. You made up 'role reversal' on the spot just to impress her.
nodes.text_bbcode: Fine. But you trying to skate by and win this scholarship [color=#e23b3b][i]is[/i][/color] an insult. You made up 'role reversal' on the spot just to impress her.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: That doesn't make it less of a topic. And I happen to `like` the idea of playing as Tybalt. His part's going to be a lot more fun than `Juliet's.`
nodes.text_bbcode: That doesn't make it less of a topic. And I happen to [color=#3b78e2][i]like[/i][/color] the idea of playing as Tybalt. His part's going to be a lot more fun than [color=#3b78e2][i]Juliet's.[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Andrew
nodes.text: Yeah, right. You don't fool me. You're not even taking this seriously. Before this, you couldn't care less about the drama club!

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Maybe I `would` have cared if pompous jerks like `you` weren't in charge.
nodes.text_bbcode: Maybe I [color=#3b78e2][i]would[/i][/color] have cared if pompous jerks like [color=#3b78e2][i]you[/i][/color] weren't in charge.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: In fact, I think I'm taking this more seriously than you.
Sam rips a poster for Andrew's production off the wall and holds it up so that Andrew can see it.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Look at these credits... You're the director, the star, and `co-`writer? Your production of 'Romeo and Juliet' might as well be called 'Romeo and Andrew's Big Fat Ego.'

nodes.text: The bell's going to ring in a minute... What do I do?

nodes.text: First, you're going to relax... When the bell rings, we're going to hand out flyers as people come in. Just smile and tell people it's a great opportunity.

nodes.text: Riiight...

nodes.text: I'm sure you all know what winning this scholarship means. Not only would you have contributed a wonderful, original vision of Shakespeare to the masses...

nodes.text: But you'll also get a four-year ride to an institution that supports the fine arts!

nodes.text: My role is to act as mentor and judge. I'll be walking you through the process and determining which production is the most worthy of the scholarship.

nodes.text: And might I say that it's delightful to work with a school putting on not one, but `two` productions of 'Romeo and Juliet'! How perfectly unique!
nodes.text_bbcode: And might I say that it's delightful to work with a school putting on not one, but [color=#3b78e2][i]two[/i][/color] productions of 'Romeo and Juliet'! How perfectly unique!

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: That's how much we love Shakespeare around here!

nodes.speaker: Ms. Macbeth
nodes.text: Wonderful. Well, I look forward to seeing the two different interpretations.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Macbeth
nodes.text: The first thing I want to do is to find out what your essay topics are going to be.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Essay? We didn't have to write anything for today, did we?

nodes.speaker: Ms. Macbeth
nodes.text: Oh no. You turn in the essay after your production is finished. But I want to know what is different about the Romeo and Juliet production that `you're` putting on.
nodes.text_bbcode: Oh no. You turn in the essay after your production is finished. But I want to know what is different about the Romeo and Juliet production that [color=#3b78e2][i]you're[/i][/color] putting on.

nodes.text: Andrew jumps in.

nodes.speaker: Andrew
nodes.text: The drama club and I are putting a new spin on 'Romeo and Juliet' as Shakespeare envisioned it. We've decided to incorporate `zombies` into the work.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Macbeth
nodes.text: Zombies?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Wait, we can `do` that? How does that not change the play?
nodes.text_bbcode: Wait, we can [color=#3b78e2][i]do[/i][/color] that? How does that not change the play?

nodes.speaker: Andrew
nodes.text: If you'd `bothered` to read the scholarship rules, you'd know that applicants must include a `creative element.` You know, the concept we have to add to the play to make it different from the original?
nodes.text_bbcode: If you'd [color=#e23b3b][i]bothered[/i][/color] to read the scholarship rules, you'd know that applicants must include a [color=#e23b3b][i]creative element.[/i][/color] You know, the concept we have to add to the play to make it different from the original?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Whoops! I didn't know we had to change the play in some way!

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Er... I knew that! I just didn't think `zombies` applied.
nodes.text_bbcode: Er... I knew that! I just didn't think [color=#3b78e2][i]zombies[/i][/color] applied.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Macbeth
nodes.text: Andrew can use the undead if he wishes. The rules only state that each applicant's 'Romeo and Juliet' production has to be an original adaptation.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Macbeth
nodes.text: You have to change an aspect of the play in some way to emphasize a theme or an idea in Shakespeare's work.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: So he can seriously put zombies in?

nodes.speaker: Andrew
nodes.text: Having zombies in my play will change the entire dynamic between Romeo and Juliet. Will death keep them separate? Or will it bring them closer `together?`
nodes.text_bbcode: Having zombies in my play will change the entire dynamic between Romeo and Juliet. Will death keep them separate? Or will it bring them closer [color=#e23b3b][i]together?[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: It's, uh...

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Maybe I can say something to get on Ms. Macbeth's good side... What were the things she loved about Shakespeare?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Oh, uh, my creative element has to do with...

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: His work has really inspired me to perform.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: It's sad that I didn't really discover this passion until now...

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: But better late than never, I say.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Macbeth

nodes.text: I don't understand... What didn't you like? Was it his inspiring prose? His complicated, three-dimensional characters? His innovative plots or ingenious narrative twists?

nodes.text_bbcode: Well, unlike [color=#e23b3b][i]some[/i][/color] people, I've devoted a great deal of time and energy to the drama club.

nodes.text: I'm Sam, and I'm athletic. I used to be on the cheerleading team, but quit that in favor of swimming.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: What you'd said before made sense, but I'm not sure about this one.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Playing 'Juliet' in a one-off play isn't going to be as useful as breaking the national high school record for swimming.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Well, definitely not when you put it like that...

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Now if we're done here... I'd like to make sure Emily gets her full practice in since she was late.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Why is that important?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: It's the most important part of it, Coach Kessler... If she's only done swimming her entire life, how will she know what makes her happy?

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: I'm not sure I like the idea of her questioning swimming as her passion. What if she quits?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Well, that is a risk... But if acting is her true passion, then she probably shouldn't be swimming anyway.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: And on the other hand, if she hates acting, she'll be able to say definitely that swimming is for her. Her one true passion.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Uh... Put this on her resume?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Not only is she learning a play that will be assigned reading next year...

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: But she's also gaining the valuable skill of speaking in front of an audience with confidence.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Does she need that skill?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Well, if she's going to be famous, she'll probably be giving press conferences and speeches. Why not start now?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: And she can also...

options.label: Determine whether acting is for her!

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: 'Fun' is not the criteria by which I judge my daughter's extracurriculars.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: If she wants to have 'fun', she has friends to hang out with.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: She doesn't have to make a commitment that will take several hours of practice out of her week.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Now if we're done here...

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: You mean, her college? Because Emily's swimming is her ticket to a full scholarship.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: No, beyond that. I'm talking about her future...

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: All right. You've got my attention. Go on.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Emily should join my stage production because it's...
Coach Kessler shakes his head.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Emily won't have to worry about getting into college if she plays her cards right and swims well.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: She's on track to be a professional athlete. Any college would kill to have her.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Now if we're done here... She has practice to start.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: This is going to be great! You play all the parts so well!

nodes.text: Now that `that's` settled, let's try again from Juliet's line... Emily, will you--
nodes.text_bbcode: Now that [color=#3b78e2][i]that's[/i][/color] settled, let's try again from Juliet's line... Emily, will you--

nodes.text: $ZOE is cut off by the slamming of the doors in the back. Coach Kessler walks down the aisle towards the stage.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Eep! Dad!

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: `Coach.` You were supposed to be in the pool twenty minutes ago!
nodes.text_bbcode: [color=#e23b3b][i]Coach.[/i][/color] You were supposed to be in the pool twenty minutes ago!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Oh, no!

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: What? The swim team has practice?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: No, it's just personal training...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Dad, I'm sorry! I didn't realize auditions would go so long...

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: I can `see` that... And what are you doing onstage in that ridiculous curtain?
nodes.text_bbcode: I can [color=#e23b3b][i]see[/i][/color] that... And what are you doing onstage in that ridiculous curtain?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: It's a bolt of cloth... And, Dad, you see... I'm in this play.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: You absolutely are not.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: `Coach.` Can we talk about this later?
nodes.text_bbcode: [color=#3b78e2][i]Coach.[/i][/color] Can we talk about this later?

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: You shirk off training without telling me like an immature teenager, and then you want to have an open conversation about this?

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: How can you expect me to treat you with respect when you don't respect the time we've set aside for your future?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: `Coach...`
nodes.text_bbcode: [color=#3b78e2][i]Coach...[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Fine. We'll talk about it during your `practice.`
nodes.text_bbcode: Fine. We'll talk about it during your [color=#e23b3b][i]practice.[/i][/color]

nodes.text: Emily steps offstage, looking sadly at Sam.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: So... Do you think she'd be able to come back?

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Just because I've realized that her social life has afforded her a certain focus doesn't mean I want her `further` distracted from her swimming.
nodes.text_bbcode: Just because I've realized that her social life has afforded her a certain focus doesn't mean I want her [color=#e23b3b][i]further[/i][/color] distracted from her swimming.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Joining the theater is a waste of her time, as far as I'm concerned.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Come along, Emily.
They walk off.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Now what can go wrong?
Ben approaches them.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I'm sorry to say this, Sam, but I wouldn't feel comfortable acting as Romeo if Emily isn't Juliet.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Great. That's just fantastic. We can change the play from Romeo and Juliet to Nurse and Mercutio!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: It just wouldn't feel right to me. You understand, right?

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: We do... But we only have half an hour until the cast list is due... What should we do now?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Stay here, Ben. I'm going to have a talk with Coach Kessler. Any advice?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Uh... He doesn't like jokes, and he doesn't believe in fun.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I know. Wait here. I'll be back.
You are now playing as Sam.
Sam bursts out of the auditorium and races to the swim center.
Coach Kessler is writing things down on his clipboard while he waits for Emily to change in the locker rooms.

nodes.text: Coach Kessler? If I could have a word?
He looks up.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: What do you want, Sam?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Look, Coach, you pulled Emily out of my auditions fast. Let me explain the situation to you.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I'd like to have Emily join my production of Shakespeare. She's a `great` actress.
nodes.text_bbcode: I'd like to have Emily join my production of Shakespeare. She's a [color=#3b78e2][i]great[/i][/color] actress.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Absolutely not.
In the face of his resistance, Sam nearly backs down...
But then she thinks of all her dreams and what she wants... And she sets her teeth.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Coach Kessler, Emily's acting may seem like a distraction to you, but it's something that will help her later.

nodes.text: This is about Emily's...

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: So if Colt is `arrogant`, then he can be the honest Friar Lawrence.
nodes.text_bbcode: So if Colt is [color=#3b78e2][i]arrogant[/i][/color], then he can be the honest Friar Lawrence.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: If Erik is `truthful,` he'll probably make the best `swordsman` Mercutio.
nodes.text_bbcode: If Erik is [color=#3b78e2][i]truthful,[/i][/color] he'll probably make the best [color=#3b78e2][i]swordsman[/i][/color] Mercutio.

nodes.text: And if Spencer is `athletic`, then he can be the `proud` Count Paris.
nodes.text_bbcode: And if Spencer is [color=#3b78e2][i]athletic[/i][/color], then he can be the [color=#3b78e2][i]proud[/i][/color] Count Paris.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I don't know if that's right...

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: But you are the casting director...

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Whatever. The roles can't matter that much in the end. As long as they get the lines right...

nodes.text: Let's have everyone run through the roles, and we'll see how it goes.

nodes.text_bbcode: Oh! I'm supposed to [color=#e23b3b][i]draw my sword[/i][/color] when it says 'Draws sword.' How silly.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Ah! Nerd attack!
Erik and Spencer go down in a flail of arms. When they try to stand up again, Erik has broken his glasses, and there's a large bruise on Spencer's face.

nodes.text_bbcode: And if [color=#e23b3b][i]I[/i][/color] don't get to sword fight, then why am I even here?

nodes.text: Erik and Spencer leave... Sam sighs, cradling her head in her hands.

nodes.speaker: Sam

$ZOE hangs her head, unsure of what to do... Her cousin's future in her hands...
And she knows with quiet certainty...
She has failed.

nodes.text: Even Ryan?

nodes.text: So... What do you think?

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: It's clear that Ben and Emily are Romeo and Juliet. Their chemistry is amazing!

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Yeah, amazingly nauseating!

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Isn't that a bad thing?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Not in a `romantic` play. What do you think of the others?
nodes.text_bbcode: Not in a [color=#3b78e2][i]romantic[/i][/color] play. What do you think of the others?

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Well... We're going to have an inexperienced cast. But if we match everyone to the right roles, I think we'll be okay.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: What do you suggest?

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Kimi will probably make a good Nurse character.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Amanda can be Romeo's mother, Lady Montague. She doesn't have very many lines, and she's mostly surprised throughout the entire thing.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Taylor can be Juliet's mother, Lady Capulet. She's mostly upset at Juliet. I think Taylor can pull off 'upset' pretty well.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I don't know when Taylor `isn't` pulling off upset.
nodes.text_bbcode: I don't know when Taylor [color=#3b78e2][i]isn't[/i][/color] pulling off upset.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: What do you think about the boys?

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: That's tougher. The male characters have a bigger role than the female characters.

nodes.text: I think Colt, Erik, and Spencer are our best bets for these roles. But which one should be which?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: We can't just do a random shuffle?

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Since no one here has formal experience, we have to make sure they are the right characters, so it's easy for them to act out the role.

nodes.text: Take a deep breath... Think of a happy place...

After the cast sheet is turned in, everyone streams out of the theater and heads home...
Everyone, that is, except for Kimi.
Kimi sits on the stage, swinging her legs as she looks out over the empty auditorium.
`O, Romeo, Romeo... Wherefore art thou, Romeo? Deny thy father and refuse thy name...`
Great. `Now` I remember the stupid line...
She's just about to hop off when she hears the sound of squeaky sneakers behind her.
Hey, Kimi, what are you doing up here?
Oh, you know... I can never get enough of sitting in dark, lonely auditoriums by myself.
I'm sitting here because I figure this is the closest I'll ever get to being front and center onstage.
Might as well live it up.
Kevin sits down next to her, dangling his legs over the lip of the stage.
This seems pretty sweet to me.
Yeah well, it's probably sweeter if you're acting onstage instead.
Are you upset because you were passed over for Juliet?
Pretty much as obvious as a moose in a bikini.
It just seemed like it'd be a fun thing to do. It's an honor to get cast in something.
Not that anyone would come to see me after what happened right before Homecoming...
Turns out, when you put a bunch of guys' names in a spreadsheet and rate their personality, no one wants to be your friend.
But it was kind of nice to dream about.
Well, I'm sorry to hear that you didn't make the cut.
But you are the Nurse, aren't you?
And we all know that nurses are hotter than noble ladies...
Ha ha... If you say so...
And far away, in Monarch Prep's detention center...
Paige tries to put in another call on the contraband cell phone she acquired from another inmate...
For one brief second, Paige hears a click and thinks someone might have picked up...
But a disappointing automated voice chirps back at her instead.
I finally have a frikkin' cell phone, and it doesn't call out?!
She thinks of the girl that gave it to her and grinds her teeth.
That... That witch! No one does this to me!
She sits on her bed, cradling her head in her hands.
Or at least they never would have before...
Just which 'witch' is Paige talking about? And what happened to Paige since Valentine's Day? Find out soon in Surviving High School!
